record.paper_title: Open problems in Gaussian fluid queueing theory
record.original_question: For fractional Brownian motion B_H with Hurst parameter H, is the associated classical Pickands constant equal to 1/Γ(1/(2H))? That is, does the identity H_{B_H} = 1/Γ(1/(2H)) hold for the full range of H under consideration?

evidence.quote: The case of fractional Brownian motion (FBM): X(t) = BH (t), where BH (·) is a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H ∈ [1/2, 1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B_H = (B_H(t))_{t \ge 0}$ be a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in [1/2, 1)$, i.e., the centered Gaussian process with stationary increments, almost surely continuous sample paths, $B_H(0) = 0$, and covariance
$$\mathrm{Cov}(B_H(s), B_H(t)) = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(|s|^{2H} + |t|^{2H} - |t-s|^{2H}\bigr).$$
The classical Pickands constant associated with $B_H$ is defined by
$$\mathcal{H}_{B_H} \;=\; \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T}\, \mathbb{E}\!\left[\exp\!\left(\sup_{t \in [0,T]} \bigl(\sqrt{2}\, B_H(t) - t^{2H}\bigr)\right)\right],$$
the limit being known to exist and to lie in $(0, \infty)$.

Decide whether the identity
$$\mathcal{H}_{B_H} \;=\; \frac{1}{\Gamma\!\bigl(1/(2H)\bigr)}$$
holds for every $H \in [1/2, 1)$.
artifact.category_tag: Pickands constants for fractional Brownian motion
artifact.status_search_result: The folklore identity $\mathcal{H}_\alpha = 1/\Gamma(1/\alpha)$ (with $\alpha = 2H$) was disproved by A. J. Harper (Bernoulli, 2017; arXiv:1404.5505) for all sufficiently small $\alpha$, where he showed $\mathcal{H}_\alpha \ge (1.1527)^{1/\alpha}/\Gamma(1/\alpha)$. This corresponds to $H$ close to $0$, outside the range $H \in [1/2,1)$ for standard fractional Brownian motion. For the actual Hurst range $H \in [1/2,1)$ (equivalently $\alpha \in [1,2)$) the conjecture has not been confirmed nor refuted; simulation evidence is often cited as suggesting it is not exact, but no rigorous resolution in this range appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Pickands' constant H_α does not equal 1/Γ(1/α), for small α
status_evidence.snippet: Harper proves that the conjectured formula H_α = 1/Γ(1/α) fails for all sufficiently small α, and gives an explicit lower bound exceeding 1/Γ(1/α).
status_evidence.claim: The folklore identity is false in general (for small α = 2H), so the conjecture in its full generality is refuted.

status_evidence.title: Pickands' constant H_α does not equal 1/Γ(1/α) (Bernoulli journal)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of Harper's disproof of the folklore conjecture for small α.
status_evidence.claim: The disproof applies to small α only, leaving the range α ∈ [1,2) (i.e. H ∈ [1/2,1)) unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Pickands' constant at first order in an expansion around Brownian motion
status_evidence.snippet: Perturbative expansion of H_α around α = 2 (Brownian case) yields corrections incompatible with 1/Γ(1/α).
status_evidence.claim: Analytic/perturbative evidence suggests the equality does not hold for H slightly less than 1, but this is not a rigorous proof in the relevant range.
